name: Bryggen
description: Bryggen is the old waterfront of Bergen, Norway, where rows of narrow, brightly painted wooden buildings face the Vågen harbour. From about 1350 it was the hub of Hanseatic merchants trading in Norway. Fires have repeatedly destroyed it, most recently in 1955, yet it was rebuilt using traditional methods. About 62 buildings survive, and today they hold museums, shops and restaurants.
